data:
CommaRh is a Rhino 8 toolkit for inspection, modeling, drafting, and CAD/IFC exchange. Run commaMenu and choose a group: Doc, Curve, Surface, Brep, Mesh, Drafting, CAD, or IFC.
Panel actions stay inside their panels. This guide lists the public commands only.
Install from the Rhino Package Manager. To report a problem, open Issues.
Brep tools. Open them from commaMenu → Brep.

Where to find it: commaMenu → Brep → uCombineNurbs.
Rebuild direction-matched Brep/surface edges and create combined loft surfaces.

Where to find it: commaMenu → Brep → uFaceFromDirection.
Extract Brep faces by direction.

Where to find it: commaMenu → Brep → uLoftPro.
Preview multi-rail Loft/Sweep output with section distribution and optional capping.

Where to find it: commaMenu → Brep → uScaleBrep.
Scale Brep geometry.

Where to find it: commaMenu → Brep → uSmoothPolySrf.
Smooth polysurface edges.
DWG and AutoCAD exchange. Open these commands from commaMenu → CAD.

Where to find it: commaMenu → CAD → uDwg.
DWG and AutoCAD bridge tools.

Where to find it: commaMenu → CAD → uDwgExport.
Batch export DWG/3DM/DXF in Object or Layer mode.

Where to find it: commaMenu → CAD → uDwgImport.
Import CAD with options.

Where to find it: commaMenu → CAD → uRegen.
Regenerate CAD geometry.
Curve tools. Open them from commaMenu → Curve.

Where to find it: commaMenu → Curve → uFlipCrv.
Flip curve direction by vector, axis, or guide curve.

Where to find it: commaMenu → Curve → uPolyToNurbsCurve.
Replace polylines with cubic interpolated curves after filtering vertices by tolerance.

Where to find it: commaMenu → Curve → uScaleCrvAtt.
Scale a curve at a specific point.

Where to find it: commaMenu → Curve → uTryGetCircle.
Fit selected curves as circles or endpoint-preserving arcs within document absolute tolerance.
Document panels and settings. Open them from commaMenu → Doc.

Where to find it: commaMenu → Doc → uAttribute.
Prioritize Layer, Name, Color, and user attributes; toggle Area/Volume with mm/m display when needed.

Where to find it: commaMenu → Doc → uLayer.
Open Comma Layer; layer actions remain in the panel.

Where to find it: commaMenu → Doc → uMove.
Open saved real/local coordinate move panel.

Where to find it: commaMenu → Doc → uObject.
Open Object inspection and Select Similar panel.

Where to find it: commaMenu → Doc → uQuickTools.
Show Quick Tools at the cursor.

Where to find it: type uQuickToolsConfig. This command is not listed on commaMenu.
Configure Quick Tools.

Where to find it: commaMenu → Doc → uScopeBox.
Create a scope box for view clipping.

Where to find it: commaMenu → Doc → uSort.
Open the saved selection-order toolbar; sort and bake actions remain in the panel.

Where to find it: commaMenu → Doc → uTolerance.
Temporarily override absolute tolerance while commands run.
Section, annotation, hatch, and measurements. Open them from commaMenu → Drafting.

Where to find it: commaMenu → Drafting → u3dSlope.
Check 3D slope.

Where to find it: commaMenu → Drafting → uAngle.
Measure an angle.

Where to find it: commaMenu → Drafting → uAnnotation.
Open annotation toolbar for scale, style, and sync.

Where to find it: commaMenu → Drafting → uArea.
Calculate surface area.

Where to find it: commaMenu → Drafting → uDiffZ.
Check Z difference between two points.

Where to find it: commaMenu → Drafting → uDist.
Measure distance between two points.

Where to find it: commaMenu → Drafting → uFindCreateBlock.
Find rigidly translated or rotated copies of selected geometry and convert them to one block.

Where to find it: commaMenu → Drafting → uGap.
Find gaps between curves.

Where to find it: commaMenu → Drafting → uLength.
Measure curve length.

Where to find it: commaMenu → Drafting → uLevel.
Check Z level.

Where to find it: commaMenu → Drafting → uMergeHatch.
Merge multiple hatches.

Where to find it: commaMenu → Drafting → uSection.
Create section curves.

Where to find it: commaMenu → Drafting → uSlope.
Slope in plane: run=X, rise=Y in World or CPlane.

Where to find it: commaMenu → Drafting → uVolume.
Calculate solid volume.
Install CommaRh, open the menu, and check the license on this computer.

CommaRh installs from Rhino’s Package Manager. There is no separate installer to download.
Open Rhino 8 on Windows. Run PackageManager. Search for CommaRh. Click Install. This guide matches CommaRh 26.1.8. Package Manager shows the version that is installed.
After install, run commaMenu.

Where to find it: commaMenu → License Manager, or type commaRegister.
commaRegister opens Comma License Manager for this computer. It shows the Machine ID (with Copy), the current status, and a license key box.
A computer without a key runs a 45-day trial. No sign-up is required. The customer line then reads “This computer (no sign-up)”. Status reads Trial with the days left, Trial - last day on the final day, Licensed for an active Pro key, or Unlicensed when the trial is over and no key is active.
To activate a key, paste it into License key or use Browse…, then click Activate. Remove clears the key stored on this computer.
For Pro, more seats, or a key for another computer, use Contact us to get a license or write to comma3d.aec@gmail.com.
Do not paste a license key into a GitHub issue.

Problems are tracked on CommaRh Issues.
Include:
The installed CommaRh version shown in Package Manager The Rhino 8 version The command name What you expected and what happened Leave license keys out of the issue. For a new key, use commaRegister or comma3d.aec@gmail.com.

Run commaMenu to open the type menu.
Group What it covers Doc Layers, objects, attributes, visibility, sort, scope box, tolerance, quick tools Curve Curve scale, direction, conversion, and circle or arc fitting Surface Surface normal Brep Scale, loft, smooth, combine, and face extraction Mesh Patch, mesh to NURBS, and 2D outline Drafting Blocks, section, annotation, hatch, and measurements CAD DWG import and export IFC IFC import, export, template, shared parameters, and IfcOpenShell commaMenu also includes License Manager, which runs commaRegister.
Commands that are not on the menu are still public. Type the command name. Each of those pages says so.
IFC exchange. Open these commands from commaMenu → IFC.

Where to find it: commaMenu → IFC → uIfcApplySharedParams.
Apply IFC.SharedParam.*[Type]. The type is in the Key (YesNo or IfcBoolean, IfcIdentifier, …) and the Value is user data.
Document shared parameters use IFC.SharedParam.<ObjectKey>[Type]. Object User Text uses <ObjectKey>[Type]. Export strips the […] from the property name and writes an IfcPropertySingleValue with that nominal type.
Right: Dimensions.QTO.Area[Area] = 12.5 Right: Pset_WallCommon.IsExternal[YesNo] = False Right: Spec.Code[IfcIdentifier] = W-01 Wrong: Spec.Flag = True[IfcBoolean]Token in […] IFC nominal value Example value Text / IfcLabel IfcLabel Sample label IfcText IfcText a long string IfcIdentifier IfcIdentifier ID-001@tag YesNo / IfcBoolean IfcBoolean Yes / True / False IfcLogical IfcLogical True Integer / IfcInteger IfcInteger 42 Number / IfcReal IfcReal 3.14 Length / IfcLengthMeasure IfcLengthMeasure 1.25 (metres) Area / IfcAreaMeasure IfcAreaMeasure 12.5 Volume / IfcVolumeMeasure IfcVolumeMeasure 0.75 IfcDate IfcDate 2026-11-07 IfcDateTime IfcDateTime 2026-11-07T16:00:00 IfcTime IfcTime 16:00:00 IfcDuration IfcDuration P1D IfcURIReference IfcURIReference https://… IfcDescriptiveMeasure IfcDescriptiveMeasure approx 2 m IfcTimeStamp IfcTimeStamp unix seconds uIfcSetupTemplateFile creates TypeCatalog_Sample with one key for each token.

Where to find it: commaMenu → IFC → uIfcExport.
Export selected objects to IFC. Default SitePlacement=Local (OpenBIM). The command seeds missing SitePlacement / MapConversion values into Document User Text.
Run uIfcSetupTemplateFile before a serious export. It seeds the layer tree and the standard Document User Text keys. Check or edit those keys in Document Properties → User Text.
Key Default Meaning IFC.SitePlacement Local Site Z = 0. Engineering elevation stays on the object. Storey Placement Z is the storey Elevation. Anchor, Mean, and Legacy anchor the site at the mean XYZ (older behavior). IFC.Storey.{Building}.{Storey}.Elevation or IFC.Storey.{Storey}.Elevation min Z if unset Storey elevation. The name must match segment 4 of the layer path. IFC.MapConversion.Eastings / Northings / OrthogonalHeight seeded when Local and empty or 0 Georeference. 0 or missing means unset, so a Local export writes mean XY / mean Z (or IFC.Offset.Z). IFC.Offset.X / Y / Z 0 Geometry offset. Independent of MapConversion. IFC.Schema IFC4 IFC4, IFC2X3, or IFC4X3. IFC.UseBridge off True with schema IFC4X3 uses IfcBridge / IfcBridgePart. If the file was not set up yet, uIfcExport reads the selected Project::Site::Building::Storey::… layer tree and writes only the Document User Text keys that are still missing. It does not overwrite existing values. After the export, open Document Properties → User Text to edit them.
Property types live in the key. See uIfcApplySharedParams.

Where to find it: commaMenu → IFC → uIfcImport.
Import IFC with options.

Where to find it: commaMenu → IFC → uIfcInstall.
Install IfcOpenShell for Rhino Python.

Where to find it: commaMenu → IFC → uIfcSetupTemplateFile.
Create an IFC template: layer hierarchy, Document User Text (including IFC.SitePlacement=Local), built-in shared parameters, and samples.
The layer tree is Project::Site::Building::Storey::…. Document User Text also receives IFC.SharedParam.*[Type]. The command creates a TypeCatalog_Sample object with one sample key for each property-type token.
Run this command before a serious IFC workflow, then review Document Properties → User Text. The key table and the export fallback are on uIfcExport.
Mesh tools. Open them from commaMenu → Mesh.

Where to find it: commaMenu → Mesh → uMeshOutline.
Extract 2D outline polylines from surfaces, polysurfaces, or meshes (CPlane / World / View; Merge All / ByLayer / PerObject).

Where to find it: commaMenu → Mesh → uMeshPatch.
Patch mesh from closed boundaries using tensile or Laplacian relaxation.

Where to find it: commaMenu → Mesh → uMeshToNurbs.
Convert meshes to NURBS; keeps attributes. Quality Fast/Balanced/Tight (default Balanced: faceted + analytic for prism/tubes/circular holes, auto-heal). Output Replace/Copy. Advanced=Yes shows Mode/Method/Tolerance/HealOpen/…. Free/Trial: 50 meshes per run. Rotational parts (bolts, shafts, rings) become real cylinders/cones; multi-piece meshes convert piece by piece and unconvertible pieces stay meshes (PARTIAL).
Public commands that are not listed on commaMenu. Type the command name.
Type commaMenu to open the compact type-based context menu. License Manager is on this menu and runs commaRegister.

Where to find it: type uExportBox. This command is not listed on commaMenu.
Clip-box parallel mesh export.

Where to find it: type uVisibilityAdd. This command is not listed on commaMenu.
Add objects to an open Visibility panel.
Surface tools. Open them from commaMenu → Surface.

Where to find it: commaMenu → Surface → uFlipSrf.
Flip surface normal by vector, axis, or guide curve.
